title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters can control event production tools
summary: The briefing's rollout dates, organiser opt-in behaviour and governance controls are supported. Two minor corrections remain: cite the shared-content documentation and acknowledge the discrepancy between the join-verification guide and the PowerShell reference.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin switch or per-person admin restriction for production-control assignment.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Who has control of production tools admin policy PowerShell Microsoft Graph production control; "production" "Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy". Opened plan-events (Admins: No control), Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy and presenter-role-reduction; no assignment restriction documented.

claims.claim: The planning page lists no admin control over inviting external presenters.
claims.quote: External presenters | No control. | Can invite presenters from outside of your organization.

claims.claim: External presenters whose identities are unverified are treated as anonymous users.
claims.quote: In Teams events hosted by your organization, external presenters whose identities aren't verified are treated as anonymous users in the event.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Join verification controls whether anonymous and unverified external presenters must verify their identity before joining.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control whether anonymous and unverified external presenters must verify their identity before joining events.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed how join verification applies to the new federated and guest production-control scenario.
claims.quote: Searched: "production control" "verification" Teams external. Opened events-external-presenter-join-verification, plan-events and events-licensing; they describe presenter verification but not production-control assignment or its specific federated/guest interaction.

claims.claim: The sources do not specify additional data access granted by external production control.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external production control presenters permissions data access. Read roadmap, MC1443517, plan-events, Control town hall production tools and Manage what attendees see; none specifies additional external-controller data access.

claims.claim: The feature comparison lists Who has control of production tools for events optimised for large audiences, not Events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: Columns: Meetings | Events up to 1,000 attendees | Events optimized for large audiences. Who has control of production tools: x | x | checkmark.

claims.claim: For Specific people, participants must already be added to the town hall to appear in the search field.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The organiser path is Calendar > town hall > View event > Manage event > Meeting options > Production tools > Who has control of production tools.
claims.quote: Select Calendar ... Select a town hall. ... Select View event > Manage event ... Select Meeting options ... In Production tools ... Who has control of production tools

claims.claim: No API or events-policy parameter is documented for assigning production control.
claims.quote: Searched: "production" "Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy"; "production tools" "Graph". Opened Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy, Graph beta virtualEventTownhall and virtualEventSettings; none exposes a production-control assignment parameter or property.

claims.claim: Join verification is configured in Teams admin center at Meetings > Events policies > policy > Verify external presenters before joining an event.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... In the Verify external presenters before joining an event dropdown list

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires external-presenter verification.
claims.quote: To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP
claims.fix: Append to the join-verification row note: 'The join-verification guide documents this command; the Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference still labels the policy preview and does not list -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification (November 2026).' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamseventspolicy for that discrepancy.

claims.claim: The join-verification policy defaults to No verification needed.
claims.quote: No verification needed | None | This is the default value. When organizers with this policy create events, they can decide whether external presenters must verify their identity before joining.

claims.claim: Large-audience event creation is configured at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents affected organisers creating events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.claim: Changing the event-creation setting to Off after scheduling prevents the user running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.where: controls[1].scope; controls[2].scope; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The two events-policy controls are user-level policies governing events created by assigned organisers.
claims.quote: User-level policy for tenant admin to configure options for customizing Teams events experiences. Use this cmdlet to update an existing policy.

claims.claim: The listed policy controls govern joining and event creation rather than selecting external production controllers.
